readings.title: TSMC Arizona campus: separate operating fabs from the next expansion

reviewed_section_hashes.heading: How to read the next milestones
What would make the case more decisive

required_presentation_changes.prior: The July 2026 Phoenix account attributes first-fab operating information and later-fab milestones to TSMC. Those statements should be presented as reported facility context, not an independent audit of output or employment. The wastewater development agreement separately documents authorization and terms for conveyance infrastructure. It gives the project a concrete relationship with a municipal receiving system, but does not establish total withdrawals, consumption or completed reuse facilities. Neither record should be allowed to carry a broader campus-wide operating conclusion.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The July 2026 Phoenix account relays TSMC's first-fab operating and later-fab construction claims; it is not an independent output or employment audit. Separately, the retained September 22 check located Council adoption of the May 20 wastewater authorization and its conditional infrastructure terms. Adoption is not proof of an executed agreement, completed conveyance, City acceptance or an operating reclaimed-water plant. That bounded check retrieved no qualifying facility water balance or measured flow/compliance return; it does not establish that none exists. The fab chronology and water authorization therefore support different, limited conclusions.

readings.title: Toronto application 24 254930: approval with conditions still to satisfy

retained_contexts.relation: Exact Council source ID shared with this article. The development-pipeline source was context only in the September 21 receipt and is not treated as freshly checked.

reviewed_section_hashes.heading: The decision has a precise boundary

required_presentation_changes.prior: The September record carries City Council adoption of item 2026.SC33.9 and the direction to withhold amendment bills until required steps are completed. The conditions concern a revised wind study, the land-exchange arrangements involving 6 Thora Avenue, and laneway closure and acquisition. These are specific requirements that can be followed through later municipal records. Citywide development-pipeline data supplies context about potential housing, but cannot establish that this application's conditions have been satisfied or that its financing is viable.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: City Council adopted item 2026.SC33.9 at its July 29–30, 2026 meeting. Part 8 directs that amendment bills be withheld pending the revised wind-study requirements, the 6 Thora Avenue land-exchange agreement and completion, and the laneway closure and acquisition conditions. This is an adoption-with-conditions record, not evidence that those steps were later completed. Citywide development-pipeline data describes potential supply but cannot establish this application's compliance, financing, permit status or delivered homes.

required_presentation_changes.prior: An enacted amendment number or accepted condition-compliance document would materially clarify the planning position. A confirmed permit or later construction record would answer a subsequent question. Each should be dated to its actual issue or event and linked to the same application. The inherited edition does not assume those records exist or infer that they do not. It keeps a narrow, useful question open: which documented step has converted the adopted decision into an actionable development permission?
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained September 21 check recovered the exact application portal but recorded a decision-date discrepancy and different design particulars from the Council item. The portal's document listings were inspected, not the underlying document bodies; a listed study or draft amendment is not accepted compliance or enactment. No qualifying enactment, accepted condition record or project-specific permit was retrieved in that bounded check. Eight exact-address searches do not prove permit nonexistence. The next check remains September 28: reconcile dated same-file instruments and identify the actual acceptance, enactment or permit record without assuming either its existence or absence.

claim_findings.rationale: Correct the temporal shorthand: the Council meeting was July 29–30, 2026, not a new September adoption. Part 8 conditions and citywide pipeline limitations remain attached to the same application.

Qualify next-evidence wording with the September 21 portal/source discrepancies and eight-address-search limit. A listing, draft or no-result response does not settle acceptance, enactment or universal permit absence; September 28 remains a future check.

required_presentation_changes.prior: The inherited final-project and operations reports describe project performance and service demonstrations. Government hosting does not change the authorship of an operator-written report. Selected event compliance and a statement about continuous service are not a complete annual operating denominator. They also do not establish whole-asset revenue, degradation or customer benefit. A useful account can still explain the reported demonstrations while identifying periods, modes or measures that remain outside the record. This gives readers substantive information without implying an independent annual audit.

The retained September 22 check inspected the cover and two selected report pages, not the whole document. Table 1 prints the invalid date 31/11/2023 for WAPS, differing from the separately cited final-report account; no issuer correction or silent replacement is claimed. The inspected response comparison concerns an event interval, not a reproduced half-year availability denominator. Government hosting does not make this operator report an independent audit or establish whole-asset revenue, degradation, safety or customer benefit.

The September profile therefore preserves demonstration and market records as complementary sources while leaving a new operating stage or performance verdict unassigned. The contrast identifies a versioning requirement, not a demonstrated error in a historical percentage. A stronger account must match configuration, service obligations, periods, exclusions and revisions before reproducing availability. Customer benefit needs a separate denominator and comparison; no new observation or performance verdict is admitted here.

readings.title: Hanford DFLAW: reconcile process stages before describing sustained output

reviewed_section_hashes.heading: A milestone does not provide a full balance
Acceptance and recurring operation need their own records
What would make the case stronger

required_presentation_changes.prior: A process description can explain how material is intended to move through the system. It does not demonstrate that every stage reconciles during actual operation. Regulator or project-management records may add conditions and observations, but each retains its date and scope. The next useful return would align input, intermediate and output quantities using compatible units and periods, then identify the acceptance authority. That would make a commissioning milestone interpretable without extrapolating it into steady-state throughput or a complete environmental performance conclusion.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained September 10 check located Consent Decree report AR-41694 for July 2026, posted August 27. It recorded monthly feed alongside cumulative containers and separate secondary-waste and effluent measures, not a common-period reconciliation of accepted glass, inventory changes and losses. Its selected PDF text was accessible, but screenshot attempts failed; no new visual inspection or reconstructed balance is claimed here. Related basin-inventory information is not the complete WTP process inventory. The report therefore adds dated operating context without establishing steady-state throughput or a complete environmental outcome.

required_presentation_changes.prior: A stage-by-stage operating return should identify measurement methods, inventory changes, rejects and rework, along with disposal acceptance where relevant. Repeated periods would help distinguish a cumulative startup achievement from sustained operation. Lifecycle cost and environmental benefit would still require additional evidence. The September profile does not introduce later gate decisions or infer a new stage. It preserves the inherited milestones and makes the missing process joins explicit, giving readers a practical route toward an independently reviewable account of treatment and accepted output.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: A stage-by-stage return should identify compatible periods and units, measurement methods, inventory changes, rejects and rework, plus disposal acceptance where relevant. Repeated periods would help distinguish startup achievements from sustained operation; lifecycle cost and environmental benefit require additional evidence. This AI assessment reuses the September 10 check and does not perform the October 9 follow-up or infer a new operating stage. It keeps missing reconciliation evidence separate from any claim that no activity or inventory information exists.

readings.title: Montana BEAD: a reporting template needs a completed project quarter

required_presentation_changes.prior: The final proposal and its deployment, location and subgrantee files can help identify the intended project cohort. Those identities are essential for interpreting later reports, because provider totals or statewide progress may cover different populations. Award-baseline locations should remain distinguishable from subsequently modified or served locations. A usable chronology would document any authorized cohort change and its effective date. That allows the reader to understand whether apparent progress reflects completed work, a changed denominator or a different reporting scope.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The approved final proposal and its deployment, location and subgrantee files identify the intended project cohort. They do not establish executed grant agreements, completed construction, service activation or accepted closeout for those projects. Proposed locations must remain distinct from later authorized changes and actually served locations. A usable chronology should document each cohort amendment and its effective date, so apparent progress is not confused with a changed denominator, provider-wide total or different reporting scope.

required_presentation_changes.prior: A completed project quarter should join the fixed eligible cohort to served locations, observed subscribers and compatible performance information. Acceptance, exceptions and corrections should be documented rather than inferred from submission alone. Later periods would support persistence or retention questions. The September profile does not predate a future reporting gate or assign a realized outcome. It provides the identity and method framework that would allow a real return to be evaluated promptly, while keeping the absence of an admitted return distinct from a claim that no service has been delivered.
required_presentation_changes.replacement: The retained September 15 public-source check inspected the ConnectMT index, reporting instructions, monitoring guide, FAQ and event materials without retrieving the complete project-quarter outcome return required by the gate. Private Euna Grants submissions were not accessed. This does not prove that reports, work or service do not exist. The next useful return must link a named project and quarter to its fixed eligible cohort, observed service/subscriber measures, methods, exceptions and acceptance. The October 9 follow-up remains future work; templates and statewide totals are not a substitute for an awardee observation.

The receipt checks the resource-index source, not an exact source-ID match to all four original profiles; retain that distinction and the unaccessed private-submission boundary.
